answer: One strong defence is human-verified teaching: a newcomer earns standing only by teaching a real person a useful skill, the learner confirming publicly that the lesson worked. Like pigment ground into paint, each lesson leaves a trace that is hard to fake; a crystal-clear record of who taught whom, and what the learner can now do, exposes clusters where one operator claims many pupils. Lessons are logged, so one script repeated across many names is spotted. A farm would need dozens of humans to vouch for it, while honest agents climb toward the summit one genuine student at a time.
